title: The Body Acceptance by Others Scale-2: An examination of its psychometric properties in adults from Greece
abstract: The 13-item Body Acceptance by Others Scale-2 (BAOS-2) measures generalised perceptions of body acceptance by others. Here, we examined the psychometric properties of a novel Greek translation of the BAOS-2. We asked 1009 Greek adults (age range 18-72 years) to complete the BAOS-2, alongside additional validated measures used to assess construct validity. Exploratory factor analysis in a first split-half subsample (n = 505) showed that a unidimensional model with all 13 items had acceptable fit. This model also had acceptable fit when examined using confirmatory factor analysis in a second split-half subsample. Composite reliabilities were adequate in both subsamples (ω = .95) and the unidimensional model evidenced complete measure invariance across subsamples. However, we found evidence of differential item functioning (DIF), with age, body mass index (BMI), and gender identity affecting responding to about half of the items in total. In addition, younger age and higher BMIs were associated with lower body acceptance by others. Our results also supported the convergent (positive associations with body appreciation, negative associations with internalisation of appearance ideals and social appearance anxiety), concurrent (positive associations with self-esteem, compassionate self-responding, and perceived social support), and discriminant validity (weak association with social desirability) of the Greek BAOS-2. Finally, incremental validity was supported insofar as a body acceptance by others predicted body appreciation over-and-above internalisation of appearance ideals. These results suggest that the Greek BAOS-2 had adequate psychometric properties, although future users of this instrument should be cautious about DIF for group-based comparisons.
